repository.name: @webex/plugin-presence
repository.purpose: Public TypeScript plugin registered as webex.presence for the presence service (catalog name apheleia). get() reads one user's composed presence; list() reads many through a Batcher that folds lookups into POST compositions; subscribe() POSTs subscriptions in batches of 50 and unsubscribe() sends subscriptionTtl 0; setStatus() POSTs events for the device user, without a label for dnd; enable(), disable(), and isEnabled() set and read the user-presence-enabled toggle through the feature plugin. Registration adds an inbound transform that copies body.eventType to body.status. An optional PresenceWorker, started by initializeWorker() or config.presence.initializeWorker, counts enqueue/dequeue watchers, fetches stale presence after a 300 ms debounce, subscribes users watched for a minute, renews watched subscriptions, listens to the Mercury event apheleia.subscription_update, expires update times after 10 minutes, and reports every change as an 'updated' event with a subscription, presence, or delete envelope. src/interface.ts types the surface; build emits declarations to dist/types. It stores nothing.

presence-public-sdk.summary: Published npm package (public plugin). main is dist/index.js, types is dist/types/index.d.ts (written by build through tsc, not by build:src), and devMain is src/index.js. Importing it imports @webex/internal-plugin-device, then registers Presence as public plugin 'presence' with config {presence: {batcherWait: 50, batcherMaxCalls: 50, batcherMaxWait: 150}} and the inbound payloadTransformer predicate and transform normalizeSingleStatusResponse; the first registration of the name wins. The entry exports only the default Presence, declared as IPresence from src/interface.ts. webex.presence exposes enable, disable, isEnabled, get, list, subscribe, unsubscribe, setStatus, initializeWorker, enqueue, dequeue, emitEvent, and the 'updated' event with {type: subscription|presence|delete, payload}; specified in src/docs/README.md.

apheleia-presence-http.source: Presence service (catalog service name apheleia, reached through api: 'apheleia' and service: 'apheleia' in src/presence.ts and src/presence-batcher.ts; route definitions are not in this repository)
apheleia-presence-http.summary: GET compositions?userId=<id> resolves one presence status object; POST compositions {subjects} resolves {statusList}; POST subscriptions {subjects, subscriptionTtl, includeStatus: true} resolves {responses: [{subject, responseCode, subscriptionTtl, status}]}, and subscriptionTtl 0 ends subscriptions; POST events {subject, eventType, label (absent for dnd), ttl} resolves a body with eventType and subject.

mercury-apheleia-subscription-update.source: Presence service push through Mercury (event name in src/constants.ts; payload definition is not in this repository)
mercury-apheleia-subscription-update.summary: Mercury envelope whose data.eventType is apheleia.subscription_update, emitted by Mercury as event:apheleia.subscription_update; the worker reads data.subject and forwards data unchanged.

webex-core-plugin-host.summary: registerPlugin keys the plugin by its raw name on WebexCore (presence, first registration wins unless replace is set, MOD-013) and merges its config and payloadTransformer entries into the module-level default config (MOD-008); WebexPlugin supplies webex, namespaced config (config.presence), trigger, and request; webex.ready and the ready event fire once the SDK is ready.

webex-core-batcher.source: @webex/webex-core Batcher (module spec consulted: packages/@webex/webex-core/src/docs/README.md MOD-050 to MOD-053; code consulted: packages/@webex/webex-core/src/lib/batcher.js)
webex-core-batcher.summary: request(item) shares one promise per fingerprint; a capped debounce flushes at most batcherMaxCalls items using batcherWait and batcherMaxWait from the subclass namespace; a WebexHttpError whose options.body has no map, or any other flush error, rejects every queued item; a response item with no pending fingerprint throws Could not find pending request for received response.

webex-core-payload-transformer.source: @webex/webex-core transform pipeline (module spec consulted: packages/@webex/webex-core/src/docs/README.md MOD-037; interceptors spec consulted: packages/@webex/webex-core/src/interceptors/docs/README.md INT-018)
webex-core-payload-transformer.summary: transform('inbound', response) runs on every inbound response and error unless the request sets disableTransform; every predicate whose direction matches is tested, and each match applies every transform with the predicate's name.

webex-core-services.summary: ServiceInterceptor maps api to service, requires resource and service, waits for the service, and joins its catalog URL with the resource.

internal-plugin-feature-toggles.source: @webex/internal-plugin-feature (workspace package, not declared in package.json; module spec consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-feature/src/docs/README.md MOD-003, MOD-004, MOD-006)
internal-plugin-feature-toggles.summary: getFeature('user', key) resolves the record value or null; setFeature('user', key, value) POSTs {key, mutable: true, val} to features/users/<userId>/user and resolves the merged record.

internal-plugin-mercury-connection.source: @webex/internal-plugin-mercury (workspace package; module spec consulted, stale on its session model: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-mercury/src/docs/README.md MOD-009; code consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-mercury/src/mercury.js)
internal-plugin-mercury-connection.summary: connected is a boolean; connect() resolves at once when connected, registers the device first otherwise, and shares one in-flight promise; an envelope with a dotted data.eventType is emitted as event, event:<namespace>, and event:<eventType>.

internal-plugin-device-identity.summary: Imported for its registration side effect. userId is a registration DTO property set from the WDM body.

lodash.summary: has tests the transform predicate path; debounce delays the worker fetch until 300 ms after the last enqueue that needs one.

internal-plugin-presence-parallel.source: @webex/internal-plugin-presence (workspace package, not a dependency; module spec consulted: packages/@webex/internal-plugin-presence/src/docs/README.md)
internal-plugin-presence-parallel.summary: Same requests, worker, config defaults, and transform name, registered as internal plugin presence; the webex bundle loads it. Both packages merge a normalizeSingleStatusResponse predicate and transform into the same default config, so a host that loads both runs the transform twice with the same result.
